en: Do not fear; the crimson banner that waves in these dawns will not fade
before the last hearth that smokes over my homeland is put out.
It is the star of my nation; it will shine;
it is mine, and it belongs to my nation alone.
Do not frown, may I be your sacrifice, O coy crescent,
smile on my heroic race! Why this violence, this wrath?
Otherwise the blood we have shed will not be lawful to you then.
Independence is the right of my nation, which worships God.
I have lived free since time began, and free I live.
What madman would put chains on me? I am astonished!
I am like a roaring flood; I trample my dam and surge over it;
I tear the mountains, I do not fit into the open expanses, I overflow.
If the horizons of the West are walled in by armour of steel,
I have a frontier like my breast full of faith.
Let it howl, do not fear! How could it strangle such a faith,
that one-toothed monster you call 'civilisation'?
Friend, do not let the vile ones reach my homeland, beware;
make your body a shield, let this shameless onslaught stop.
The days that God promised you will dawn;
who knows, perhaps tomorrow; perhaps even sooner than tomorrow.
Do not pass over the ground you tread on, calling it 'soil': know it!
Think of the thousands lying beneath it without a shroud.
You are the son of a martyr. Do not hurt your forefather, it would be a shame;
do not give this paradise of a homeland, even if you were to gain worlds.
Who would not be sacrificed for the sake of this paradise of a homeland?
Martyrs would gush out if you squeezed its soil, martyrs!
Let God take my life, my beloved, all that I have,
but let Him not part me in this world from my only homeland.
O my God, the one wish of my soul from You is this:
let no stranger's hand touch the breast of my temple.
These calls to prayer, whose testimonies are the foundation of the faith,
must ring out over my eternal homeland.
Then my gravestone, if I have one, will bow down a thousand times in ecstasy,
O my God, my bloody tears pouring from every wound of mine;
my corpse will spring from the earth like a disembodied spirit;
then, rising, my head will perhaps touch the Throne.
Wave you too like the dawns, O glorious crescent!
Let all the blood I have shed now be lawful at last.
Forever there is no perishing for you, nor for my race:
freedom is the right of my flag, which has lived free;
independence is the right of my nation, which worships God.
notes: line 1.1: 'sönmez' is 'will not go out, be extinguished', the word used of fire and light, as in line 1.2.
line 2.1: 'kurban olayım', 'may I be your sacrifice', an endearment; 'nazlı hilâl', the coy (or proud, petted) crescent of the flag.
line 2.3: 'helâl' is what is religiously lawful, and also what is given or forgiven ungrudgingly: the blood shed for the flag would not be blessed or freely given to it.
lines 2.4 and 10.5: 'Hakk' is God (the Truth, the Right), a play on 'hakkı', 'its right'.
line 3.4: 'enginler' are open plains or the open sea; 'taşarım', 'I overflow, spill over'.
line 4.4: 'tek dişi kalmış canavar', 'the monster with only one tooth left', i.e. a decrepit beast.
line 8.2: 'nâmahrem', one who is not of the family and may not enter its private quarters; 'mâbed', a temple or place of worship.
line 9.4: 'arş', the Throne of God in the highest heaven.
line 4.3: 'Ulusun' is read as 'let it howl' (ulumak, to howl), said of the monster of the next line.
